back: Extracts natural resources: farming, mining, fishing, forestry.
Turns raw materials into goods: manufacturing and construction.
Provides services, e.g. transport, banking, insurance, retailing, education, health.
Commercial services (trade and aids to trade) help goods reach consumers; direct services are given personally to people (teachers, nurses).
The stages a product passes through from raw material to the final consumer.
Each sector relies on the others for inputs, services or customers; a problem in one spreads to the others.
Transport, communication, banking, insurance, warehousing and advertising.
Employment shifts from primary to secondary and then to tertiary as incomes rise and farming is mechanised.
Construction is in the secondary sector, not the tertiary sector.
